facts.label: Version relationships and conflicts
facts.text: 1. Term loan margin. The 10-K and Q1 10-Q give SOFR plus 2.00%; the Q2 and Q3 10-Q give SOFR plus 1.75% after the Seventh Amendment: [Q2-10Q page:18] "SOFR plus a margin of 1.75% or an alternate base rate plus a margin of 0.75%". This is a dated change, not a conflict; consumers must use the Q3 terms for current pricing and the 10-K for FY2025 expense. 2. Stale amendment text inside the Q3 report. The Q3 MD&A (page:44) still introduces the term loan as "(the “Existing Term Loans”)" at "$985.0 million" maturing September 2032, while Note 10 (page:20) shows the Repriced Term Loans at a September 2032 balance of "$975,150" thousand. Note 10 is the controlling statement of the carrying amount; the MD&A description is a presentation lag, not a second instrument. Downstream use should cite Note 10 for the balance. 3. Unit error in the Q1 MD&A. [Q1-10Q page:32] "aggregate principal amount of $985.0 billion" conflicts with the same figure in millions in the Q2 and Q3 reports and in the 10-K. Treat as a typographical error; the Q1 balance sheet and Note 10 control. Downstream effect: any extraction from that sentence must be rejected. 4. Long-term debt line. The balance sheet carries long-term debt net of unamortized costs and discount (the Long-term debt, net line at September 30, 2026 on page:5 of the Q3 10-Q), while the release states approximately $975 million of debt. These are net versus gross principal measures, not a conflict, but CP-1 must state which basis it uses. 5. Description of the First Eagle transaction differs in completeness across documents: the Q3 10-Q (pages:12 to 13) and Q3 release (page:2) state the outline; the Q2 documents pre-date it (agreement dated 2026-08-25, after the Q2 release of 2026-08-05) and the Q2 10-Q was filed on 2026-08-06 per the retrieval index. The Q2 sources therefore do not contain it and must not be read as saying the transaction did not exist at their own dates of reporting.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is usable for a credit snapshot of the standalone company at September 30, 2026, with the following boundaries. The statements are consolidated and complete for the annual report and the three quarterly reports; every reported figure in the tables below is taken from a statement page, and the adjusted EBITDA reconciliations are the company's own. Debt is one instrument family: the term loan under the 2019 Credit Agreement, 975,150 thousand dollars of principal at September 30, 2026, with a 100.0 million dollar revolver that is undrawn. Standalone leverage on the company's adjusted EBITDA is low and has fallen across the four periods tested, and cash interest is covered many times; both results lean on a management EBITDA that adds back share-based compensation, acquisition and restructuring costs, so the same ratios are shown on a stricter proxy. The base cannot support three conclusions: the covenant headroom (the ratio is not reported), the capital structure after the pending First Eagle acquisition (no amounts, no financing terms), and any ratings or market view (none supplied). LTM figures are calculated, not reported, and the fiscal 2025 column carries only three quarters of the Amundi US business, which closed on April 1, 2025, so the FY2025 ratios are not comparable with the LTM ratios without that caveat.

facts.label: Capital structure and debt terms
facts.text: - Instrument: term loan under the 2019 Credit Agreement, principal 975,150 at September 30, 2026 (982,538 at December 31, 2025), maturing September 23, 2032, amortizing 1% a year of the 985.0 million dollar original principal in quarterly installments. Q3-10Q page:20 shows the table "Due September 2032$975,150" with an interest rate of 5.82% and an effective rate of 5.98%. Carrying value is 965,911 net of unamortized issuance costs of 3,014 and discount of 6,225 (Q3-10Q page:20). - Pricing: after the Seventh Amendment of May 18, 2026 the margin is SOFR plus 1.75% (alternate base rate plus 0.75%); the company elects three-month Term SOFR (Q3-10Q page:20). Before it, SOFR plus 2.00% (10-K page:142). Interest rates are floating; the swap was terminated on October 30, 2023, and its deferred gain is being amortized as a credit to interest expense through September 23, 2032 (Q3-10Q page:25), which makes reported interest expense lower than cash interest in each period; the unamortized balance at December 31, 2025 was 11.7 million dollars before tax (10-K page:145). - Revolver: 100.0 million dollar commitment with a 10.0 million dollar letter-of-credit sublimit, maturing September 23, 2030, undrawn at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025 (Q3-10Q page:44). No letter of credit is shown as using it at September 30, 2026: the liquidity table prints an undrawn commitment equal to the full 100,000 (Q3-10Q page:43). - Ranking and parties: the revolver is described as first lien; the borrower is Victory Capital Holdings, Inc.; the guarantors and collateral package are Not supplied (the filings refer only to "the other loan parties"). No other debt instrument, bond, finance lease or off-balance-sheet debt is printed in the balance sheet or debt notes. - Total debt per the Q3 earnings release is "approximately $975 million" (R3 page:4), which agrees with the gross principal in the note; the balance sheet shows the net carrying amount.

facts.label: Claims outside the debt figure
facts.text: - Operating leases: operating lease liabilities of 42,405 at September 30, 2026 (Q3-10Q page:5) and 45,610 at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:149); all leases are operating leases (10-K page:149). facts.label: Covenants
facts.text: The 2019 Credit Agreement carries one financial maintenance covenant: a first lien leverage ratio of no greater than 4.00 to 1.00, tested at the end of each fiscal quarter only when revolver borrowings exceed 35.0% of commitments (Q3-10Q page:20). With a 100.0 million dollar commitment the test is not triggered unless more than 35.0 million dollars is drawn (calculated), and the revolver is undrawn. There is no step-down printed. The company states it was in compliance at September 30, 2026. The reported covenant ratio, the covenant definition of EBITDA and first lien debt, and any add-back cap are Not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable. For orientation only, gross term loan principal over the calculated LTM adjusted EBITDA is 1.14x; this is not the covenant metric, because the covenant is defined on first lien debt and a covenant EBITDA that is not in the pack.

facts.label: Definition risks in EBITDA
facts.text: Adjusted EBITDA (US$ thousands) is the company's measure: 856,348 on an LTM basis against 727,102 for the stricter proxy of income from operations plus depreciation and amortization, a calculated difference of 129,246 that rests on the reconciliation's addbacks and is not decomposed here. The addbacks include share-based compensation, which the footnote describes as "associated with equity awards in connection with acquisitions and certain one-time performance-based shares" (Q3-10Q page:43), acquisition, restructuring and exit costs, other business taxes, and debt issuance costs. The share-based compensation addback is 32,547 in Q3 2026 against 2,022 in Q3 2025 (Q3-10Q page:42), and the filings do not separate the one-time part. On the proxy, leverage at September 30, 2026 is 1.34x gross and 1.06x net, against 1.14x and 0.90x on adjusted EBITDA. Both are far below the 4.00x covenant level, but that level is a different metric. Pro forma Amundi US data is given only for revenue and net income, not EBITDA (Q3-10Q page:12), so no pro forma EBITDA exists in the pack.

Income from operations was 137,723 against 138,126, so operating income was flat on higher revenue because operating expenses rose (258,850 against 223,069, Q3-10Q page:5), including acquisition-related costs of 15,529 in Q3 2026 against 379 (Q3-10Q page:5). - First Eagle: on August 25, 2026 the company agreed to acquire GC Ferry Holdings, Inc. ("First Eagle") by a two-step merger; consideration is "a combination of cash, newly issued shares of the Company’s common stock, and newly issued shares of a new series of the Company’s non-voting convertible preferred stock"; a debt commitment letter provides financing "to fund the cash portion of the consideration and related fees and expenses"; closing is expected by the end of the first quarter of 2027, subject to stockholder approval, regulatory approvals and client consents (Q3-10Q pages:12 and 13). No amount of consideration, cash, new debt, commitment size or pricing is disclosed in the pack. Stockholder litigation and demand letters followed the proxy filings (Q3-10Q pages:47 and 48). - Repricing: the Seventh Amendment of May 18, 2026 repriced the term loan; costs of 2.4 million dollars, of which 2.0 million dollars is a loss on debt extinguishment (Q3-10Q page:21). - Dividend: a quarterly dividend of 0.50 dollars per share approved on November 4, 2026, payable December 23, 2026 (Q3-10Q page:25). - Nothing in the pack is dated after the cutoff of 2026-11-05.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Victory Capital is a diversified, asset-based investment manager whose credit profile rests on three things the sources document. First, a fee-on-assets revenue model: revenue moves with average assets under management, the fee rate and net flows, and fund advisory agreements are cancellable on short notice, so revenue is recurring in form but not contractually locked. Second, a multi-franchise, centralized-platform structure that management says keeps about two-thirds of operating expense variable and capital spending minimal, which supports cash conversion but depends on the investment teams being retained. Third, a strategic relationship with Amundi that is at once shareholder, board-nominating party, exclusive offshore distributor and exclusive supplier of Amundi's active products into the United States, which concentrates ownership, distribution and governance in one counterparty. The consolidated company's only debt is one term loan with an undrawn revolver (CP-1); ownership has no sponsor named, but no controlling-holder register is in the pack beyond Amundi and employee ownership. The transaction that matters most to a creditor is the pending acquisition of First Eagle for cash, common shares and a new series of non-voting convertible preferred stock, financed in part by a debt commitment letter whose amount and terms are not in the pack. All views here are on the standalone, pre-First Eagle company, and every First Eagle consequence is a gap, not a conclusion.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The Amundi US transaction closed on April 1, 2025. In exchange for all the shares of Amundi's U.S. business, Victory issued 3,293,471 shares of common stock and 19,698,274 shares of preferred stock (net of 44,026 preferred shares forfeited in a post-closing adjustment on August 1, 2025, per 10-K page:109), together 26.1% of fully diluted shares; the purchase price was approximately 1,326 US$ million, settled entirely in Company shares (Q3-10Q page:11). The 10-K exhibit index lists a certificate of designations for Series A Non-Voting Convertible Preferred Stock, and Amundi may require Victory to nominate two Amundi designees to the board (10-K page:135). Alongside the equity, Victory and Amundi entered exclusive distribution agreements, a 15-year exclusive offshore distribution arrangement that auto-renews in 2040 (10-K page:14). The purchase price allocation was finalized in Q1 2026 (Q3-10Q page:12). Pioneer Investments contributed revenue of about 155 US$ million in Q3 2026 and 517 US$ million in nine months 2026, and the filing states that net income attributable to Pioneer is "impractical to determine" because discrete franchise-level financial information is not prepared (Q3-10Q page:12). The Amundi deal is a completed transaction, so for creditors it explains the 2025 jump in assets and in goodwill and intangibles, not a new financing event.

facts.text: Debt events in the period are refinancings, not new money. On September 23, 2025 the Sixth Amendment extended the revolver to September 23, 2030 and repriced the term loan at 985.0 US$ million; on May 18, 2026 the Seventh Amendment repriced the term loan to SOFR plus 1.75% (Q2-10Q page:18; Q3-10Q page:20). No bond, note or other new debt issue appears in the pack. Costs of the Seventh Amendment were 2.4 US$ million, of which 2.0 US$ million was a loss on debt extinguishment (Q3-10Q page:21).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The pending First Eagle transaction, all of it a subsequent event relative to the Q2 2026 reports and still pending at the cutoff, is described in the Q3 2026 report: on August 25, 2026 Victory agreed to acquire GC Ferry Holdings, Inc. from GC Ferry Parent, L.P. through a two-step merger; consideration is a combination of cash, newly issued common stock and a new series of non-voting convertible preferred stock; Victory entered a debt commitment letter with certain financial institutions to fund the cash portion and related fees; closing is expected by the end of the first quarter of 2027, subject to approval by Victory stockholders, regulatory approvals and client consents (Q3-10Q pages:12 and 13). Management calls it "transformational" and says it adds a scaled CLO and alternative credit platform (R3 page:2), which is Management Language. For a creditor the mechanics are: cash consideration funded by new debt raises leverage from the current low standalone level by an amount that is not disclosed; new preferred stock adds a senior-to-common claim, as the Amundi preferred already is; share issuance dilutes and may shift control, and the closing depends on stockholder and client consents, so completion risk and the post-closing capital structure are both open. Transaction costs already expensed were 15.5 US$ million in Q3 2026 and 22.5 US$ million in nine months 2026 (Q3-10Q page:13). Litigation followed the proxy: two stockholder complaints and ten demand letters seek, among other things, to enjoin closing until more disclosure is made (Q3-10Q page:48); Victory calls them without merit and gives no loss estimate. No amount of consideration, cash portion, commitment size, lenders, pricing, ticking fees or conditions of the financing is in the pack, and no First Eagle financial statements are supplied, so the new debt issue, pro forma leverage, and pro forma liquidity are Not supplied and Not calculable. Dated after the Q3 reporting period but inside the cutoff: the definitive proxy statement (October 16, 2026) and the dividend of 0.50 dollars per share approved on November 4, 2026.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Evidence: fund advisory agreements terminable on not more than 60 days' notice (10-K page:26), and revenues that "are based on the level of client assets we manage" (10-K page:16). Mechanic: assets can be withdrawn or fall with markets with little notice, so fee revenue and EBITDA fall quickly. Implication: debt service capacity is high today but is exposed to a market or performance shock; monitoring posture should track monthly flows and AUM. Counter: management says about two-thirds of operating expense is variable, which dampens margin impact. 2. Evidence: Amundi as 26.1% fully diluted holder, two board nominees, exclusive distribution (Q3-10Q page:11; 10-K page:135, page:14). Mechanic: one counterparty influences ownership, governance and the offshore revenue channel; a dispute or change could affect distribution and strategic direction. Implication: key uncertainty on counterparty dependence; creditor control is not affected as there is no sponsor, but equity ownership is partly in a preferred class with its own terms Not supplied. 3. Evidence: pending First Eagle acquisition with a debt commitment letter and cash consideration (Q3-10Q pages:12 and 13); CP-1 shows low standalone leverage on a single term loan. Mechanic: cash funded by new debt will raise debt service and leverage by an undisclosed amount, while preferred issuance adds a claim ranking ahead of common; the benefit depends on integration and net flows of an acquired platform. Implication: leverage tolerance after closing is the central open question; committee readiness is limited until the financing documents are in the pack. Counter: the conflict log has no direct conflict on the First Eagle terms, but absence of amounts is itself the limitation. 4. Evidence: net flows swung from outflow to inflow (R1 page:1; R3 page:2) and Q3 2026 revenue fell against Q2 2026 on annual fee timing (R3 page:3). Mechanic: quarterly revenue is volatile around performance and annual fees. Implication: use LTM rather than single-quarter EBITDA for any ratio, as CP-1 does.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Victory Capital's standalone credit profile is sound on every measure the sources allow, but the credit view after the First Eagle acquisition is open. The strongest support is balance sheet and cash generation: USD 975.15 million of term loan against USD 856.348 million of last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA (1.14x gross, 0.90x net), cash interest cover of 14.83x, USD 307.724 million of liquidity and a first maturity of any size in September 2032. The weakest point is that earnings are fee income on assets that clients can withdraw on short notice, and a large cash-and-shares acquisition is pending whose debt, terms and target financials are not in the sources. What decides the outcome is the size and pricing of the First Eagle financing, whether closing happens as planned, and whether net inflows persist after the record third quarter of 2026.
facts.basis: Literal wrapped paragraph from the model-authored handoff; no new analysis.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. The standalone balance sheet carries one debt instrument, the term loan under the 2019 Credit Agreement of USD 975.15 million at September 30, 2026, alongside an undrawn USD 100.0 million revolver, described as first lien, maturing September 23, 2030 [CP-1 capital structure]. The interest rate is 5.82%, floating at SOFR plus 1.75% since the May 18, 2026 repricing. Leverage on management's adjusted EBITDA fell from 1.44x at FY2025 to 1.14x at the last twelve months to Q3 2026 [CP-1 leverage chart]; the fall comes from higher EBITDA (USD 682.851 million to USD 856.348 million) and from the FY2025 figure including only three quarters of the Amundi US business, which means the comparison flatters the improvement. On the stricter proxy of operating income plus depreciation and amortization (USD 727.102 million), leverage is 1.34x gross and 1.06x net [CP-1 definition risks]. Either way leverage is far under the single covenant level of 4.00x, but that covenant is defined on first lien debt and a covenant EBITDA that are not in the sources, so headroom is Not calculable.

Management says about two-thirds of operating expense is variable, a Management Language claim, but personnel compensation rose in the third quarter of 2026, so the cushion is not proved [CP-1A operating model].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 6. First Eagle changes the credit profile. Consideration is cash, new common stock and a new series of non-voting convertible preferred stock, funded in part under a debt commitment letter; closing is expected by the end of the first quarter of 2027, subject to stockholder, regulatory and client approvals; stockholder litigation seeks to delay it [CP-1A transaction summary]. No amounts are given. Any post-closing leverage, liquidity, ranking or covenant statement is Not calculable and is withheld.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. (1) Low standalone leverage and strong cover on the sources' own measures, Documentary Fact from the CP-1 tables, with the caveat that adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that adds back share-based compensation and acquisition costs; the stricter proxy still gives a leverage level well within the covenant level. (2) A long, simple debt structure: one term loan to September 23, 2032, amortizing 1% a year, with calculated annual maturities of USD 9.85 million before the bullet of about USD 918.5 million, and a revolver to September 23, 2030 that is undrawn (Documentary Fact for the dates, Analyst Interpretation for the calculated schedule). (3) Liquidity of USD 307.724 million, with minimal capital spending of USD 3.024 million in nine months 2026 (Documentary Fact). (4) Scale and diversity across eight investment franchises, a Solutions Platform and four client channels, with the largest franchise at about 42% of assets under management (Documentary Fact). (5) Net inflows in the second and third quarters of 2026 after outflows in the first quarter of 2026 and in the nine months of 2025: USD 11.702 billion of long-term net inflows in the third quarter of 2026 (Management Language for "record", Documentary Fact for the amount).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. (1) Revenue visibility is short because fund advisory contracts can be ended on 60 days' notice and revenue moves with markets, flows and fee realization, which fell to 44.8 bp in the third quarter of 2026 from 47.9 bp in the second quarter (Documentary Fact). (2) Reliance on Amundi for ownership, board seats and offshore distribution concentrates a single counterparty (Documentary Fact); the Amundi preferred stock terms are Not supplied. (3) The pending First Eagle acquisition with undisclosed debt and a cash component creates leverage, execution and litigation risk (Documentary Fact for existence; the credit effect is Insufficient Information). (4) Earnings quality: adjusted EBITDA exceeds the proxy by USD 129.246 million (15.1% of adjusted EBITDA, calculated below), and the share-based compensation addback jumped in the third quarter of 2026 without the one-time part being separated (Documentary Fact). (5) Distributions to equity absorb most operating cash flow, leaving debt reduction at the scheduled amount (Analyst Interpretation). (6) Absent monitoring data: covenant ratio, guarantors and collateral, restricted payment capacity and ratings (Insufficient Information).

Source-readiness review (CP-0) for Victory Capital Holdings, Inc. (ticker VCTR, Delaware registrant, commission file number 001-38388), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, public case, reporting currency USD, current period Q3 2026 against prior period FY2025. The cutoff is 2026-11-05. The requested downstream consumers are CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 (minimum module set). The question is whether the supplied source set can support those consumers and what stays blocked. This handoff gives no credit conclusion, does not normalize or reconcile any figure, and asserts SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED.

Perimeter: the reporting entity is Victory Capital Holdings, Inc. "along with its wholly-owned subsidiaries" (consolidated); there is no separate borrower, parent or guarantor in the context file (borrower, parent and guarantor fields are blank, not zero). ## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on

### Supplied handoffs

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filed documents give full text coverage of the annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases. They support the four requested analyses with stated limits, mainly on the pending First Eagle acquisition and its financing. | Medium | The merger agreement, debt commitment letter, credit agreement and First Eagle financials are not in the pack. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Debt is one term loan under the 2019 Credit Agreement, plus an undrawn revolver, disclosed in the annual and quarterly reports. | Debt and liquidity inputs can be taken from audited and filed statements. | High |

| The First Eagle acquisition was signed after the second quarter and is described only in outline, with no amounts. | Pro forma leverage and the size of new debt cannot be built from this pack. | High |
| The covenant is described in words only, with no reported ratio or definition. | Covenant headroom cannot be computed from these sources. | High |
| Earnings releases give adjusted measures that the quarterly reports reconcile. | Adjusted figures are usable as attributed management measures, not as audited facts. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for each of CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5. Filed statements cover the current period (Q3 2026 and nine months 2026), the prior-period comparison (FY2025 audited, plus Q3 2025 and nine months 2025 comparatives in the Q3 report), and the debt note. The strongest contrary evidence is the pending First Eagle transaction: it is the largest forward credit event in the pack, yet its financing terms sit in documents that are listed in an exhibit index but not supplied, so any pro forma capital structure is blocked. No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED, because each owner can perform its own method on the retained filings with the gaps carried forward. Status is source sufficiency only; it does not say downstream analysis is complete or accepted.
### Per-source assessment
#### Annual report (10-K, FY2025)

The cover page identifies the registrant and period: [10-K page:1] "For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025". The debt note (Note 11) is on page:141 to page:143 and the single reportable segment disclosure is in Note 19. The 10-K gives the covenant wording and the year-end term loan at the pre-amendment margin: [10-K page:142] "SOFR plus a margin of 2.00% or an alternate base rate plus a margin of 1.00%". This margin was later lowered (see conflicts). The 10-K governs FY2025 facts; where a quarterly report restates a December 2025 balance, the 10-K is the original authority.
#### Quarterly reports (10-Q, Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026)

Each is a separate, active source; none supersedes another. The Q3 report states a prior-period revision: [Q3-10Q page:9] "Certain prior period amounts have been revised to conform to the current period presentation." That sentence says the revision had no effect on previously reported results, but the revised line items are not identified, so a prior-period comparison must read the Q3 comparatives rather than an earlier report where they differ. The Q3 report was filed on the cutoff date itself (retrieval index filing date 2026-11-05) and is inside the cutoff; its own cover states shares outstanding "as of October 30, 2026".
#### Earnings releases (Exhibit 99.1, Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026)

These are management presentations of reported and adjusted results and give attributed supporting claims only. The Q3 release states: [R3 page:4] "The total debt outstanding as of September 30, 2026 was approximately $975 million." and its non-GAAP measures are reconciled to GAAP in the Q3 10-Q: [Q3-10Q page:42] "Adjusted EBITDA$212,135$190,451$658,872$485,375". No guidance table was located in any release (the word "outlook" appears only in forward-looking-statement boilerplate). Release headlines use "Record" language (management characterisation, not adopted).
### Entity, perimeter and instrument roles

- Issuer and sole borrower named in the filings: Victory Capital Holdings, Inc. The 10-K exhibit index describes the original credit agreement with the Company "as borrower". Subsidiary guarantors are not enumerated in the supplied text: the filings say "the other loan parties party thereto" without naming them. Whether any restricted or unrestricted subsidiary distinction exists is Not supplied.

- Debt instrument: term loan and revolver under the 2019 Credit Agreement. [Q3-10Q page:20] "Due September 2032$975,150" under the heading "Term Loans". The revolver is undrawn: [Q3-10Q page:44] "which had approximately $100.0 million undrawn as of September 30, 2026".
- Amendment history is in the filings only as narrative: Fifth Amendment (2024), Sixth Amendment (2025-09-23) and Seventh Amendment (2026-05-18). The amendment documents themselves are not supplied.

- Regulated subsidiary constraint: [Q3-10Q page:45] "such subsidiaries of our Company may be restricted in their ability to transfer cash to their parents." This bears on how much consolidated cash is available at the parent; the split of cash by entity is Not supplied.

- Equity-linked holder: Amundi received common and preferred shares in the April 2025 acquisition [Q3-10Q page:11] "represented in the aggregate 26.1% of the Company’s fully diluted shares". Preferred stock is outside debt but within the capital structure the consumers must keep distinct.
### Version relationships and conflicts

1. Term loan margin. The 10-K and Q1 10-Q give SOFR plus 2.00%; the Q2 and Q3 10-Q give SOFR plus 1.75% after the Seventh Amendment: [Q2-10Q page:18] "SOFR plus a margin of 1.75% or an alternate base rate plus a margin of 0.75%". This is a dated change, not a conflict; consumers must use the Q3 terms for current pricing and the 10-K for FY2025 expense.

2. Stale amendment text inside the Q3 report. The Q3 MD&A (page:44) still introduces the term loan as "(the “Existing Term Loans”)" at "$985.0 million" maturing September 2032, while Note 10 (page:20) shows the Repriced Term Loans at a September 2032 balance of "$975,150" thousand. Note 10 is the controlling statement of the carrying amount; the MD&A description is a presentation lag, not a second instrument. Downstream use should cite Note 10 for the balance.

3. Unit error in the Q1 MD&A. [Q1-10Q page:32] "aggregate principal amount of $985.0 billion" conflicts with the same figure in millions in the Q2 and Q3 reports and in the 10-K. Treat as a typographical error; the Q1 balance sheet and Note 10 control. Downstream effect: any extraction from that sentence must be rejected.

4. Long-term debt line. The balance sheet carries long-term debt net of unamortized costs and discount (the Long-term debt, net line at September 30, 2026 on page:5 of the Q3 10-Q), while the release states approximately $975 million of debt. These are net versus gross principal measures, not a conflict, but CP-1 must state which basis it uses.

5. Description of the First Eagle transaction differs in completeness across documents: the Q3 10-Q (pages:12 to 13) and Q3 release (page:2) state the outline; the Q2 documents pre-date it (agreement dated 2026-08-25, after the Q2 release of 2026-08-05) and the Q2 10-Q was filed on 2026-08-06 per the retrieval index. The Q2 sources therefore do not contain it and must not be read as saying the transaction did not exist at their own dates of reporting.
### Coverage of source profiles

- Financial statements and notes: balance sheet, operations, comprehensive income, equity, cash flows, debt, segment (one reportable segment), subsequent events and non-GAAP reconciliation are present in the Q3 report and the 10-K. The Q3 supplemental cash flow data gives cash paid for interest and for income taxes (nine months 2026 and 2025). Discrete quarters can be obtained for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 from the three quarterly reports; Q4 2025 as a discrete quarter is Not supplied as a source (it would be a derived annual-less-nine-months figure and no Q4 2025 release is in the pack).

- Segment and KPI: AUM, flows, revenue realization and investment performance are given in the releases and the Q3 10-Q MD&A. Segment profit tables are not applicable because one reportable segment is reported. Revenue by franchise is not separated except for Pioneer Investments: [Q3-10Q page:12] "Net income attributable to Pioneer Investments for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 is impractical to determine".

- Debt and facility level: one term loan tranche and one revolver; facility-level carrying value, rates, maturity and amortization (1% a year in the 10-K, [10-K page:143] "amortize at 1% per annum") are present. Letters of credit: the revolver has a sublimit, and the liquidity table shows the full commitment undrawn, so no letters of credit are shown as using it.

- Covenants: one financial maintenance covenant in words: [Q3-10Q page:20] "of no greater than 4.00 to 1.00". The wording makes it a test that applies only when revolver borrowings exceed 35.0% of commitments; the reported first lien leverage ratio and the definition of covenant EBITDA are Not supplied.
- Liquidity: the Q3 10-Q MD&A (page:43) gives a liquidity table with cash, receivables and undrawn commitment. Cash taxes and interest paid are in the cash flow statement.
- Presentations and decks: none in the pack; releases substitute for quarterly presentations. No image or chart content was relied on, and none is claimed as inspected.
- Workbooks and legal documents: none supplied (context legal_documents is none).
### Readiness by consumer
| Consumer | Status | Evidence located | Limitations carried forward |

| CP-1 (financial data extraction and metrics) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Three statements, notes, debt table, cash paid for interest and taxes, adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, discrete Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 and FY2025 | Q4 2025 discrete quarter not supplied; covenant ratio and definition not supplied; Q1 unit typo; MD&A debt text lags Note 10; pro forma First Eagle figures not available |

| CP-1A (business and transaction context) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business description in the 10-K, Amundi US acquisition notes, First Eagle outline in Q3 note 3, Item 1 legal proceedings, subsequent events | Merger agreement, debt commitment letter, proxy statement and First Eagle financials not supplied; consideration split and cash amount not located; ownership detail beyond the Amundi stake limited |
| CP-2 (fundamental credit synthesis) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Inherits CP-1 and CP-1A evidence | Cannot size post-transaction leverage or liquidity; no ratings or market data supplied |

| CP-5 (evidence trace validator) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Full text of all seven sources permits quote matching | Carries every limitation above; releases are management claims and must not override filings |
No consumer is conditional or blocked, so none is marked DO NOT RUN.
### Subsequent events and dated items

Inside the cutoff: the First Eagle agreement dated August 25, 2026 and the related proxy filings ([Q3-10Q page:47] "On October 2, 2026, Victory filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) a preliminary proxy statement") and stockholder litigation ([Q3-10Q page:48] "Wright v. Victory Capital Holdings, Inc., et al., Index No. 656101/2026"); the dividend approved on November 4, 2026 ([Q3-10Q page:25] "payable on December 23, 2026"). The expected close is a forward-looking term: [Q3-10Q page:13] "expected to close by the end of the first quarter of 2027". It is a contract expectation, not a fact that has occurred. Nothing in the pack is dated after 2026-11-05.
## Calculations

None. CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. The page and source coverage counts are taken directly from the pack: the seven sources hold 165, 37, 46, 50, 13, 15 and 17 pages, and every page of each was inspected as text. No derived financial amount is stated in this handoff; every dollar figure above is quoted from a source at the locator given.
## Gaps

| Agreement and Plan of Merger dated 2026-08-25 listed as Exhibit 2.1 in the Q3 10-Q exhibit index but not in the pack | High | CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5 | Add the Exhibit 2.1 text to the pack |

| Definitive proxy statement filed October 16, 2026 (referred to in Q3 10-Q Part II Item 1), not supplied; likely holds pro forma and consideration details | High | CP-1A, CP-2 | Add the proxy statement |
| First Eagle standalone financials, AUM and cash flow: Not supplied | High | CP-2 | Add the proxy statement or First Eagle financial statements |

## Next module

CP-1 (financial data and metrics) runs next, then CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 in dependency order. CP-1 should take FY2025 from the 10-K and Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 and nine months from the quarterly reports; cite Note 10 for the term loan balance; label cash interest and cash taxes by period; treat release figures as attributed management measures; keep gross principal and net carrying value distinct; flag that covenant headroom and pro forma First Eagle leverage are Not calculable from this pack. CP-1A should carry the First Eagle gaps into the transaction summary, and CP-5 should check every claim against the cited page, rejecting extractions from the Q1 unit-error sentence.

Financial base extraction and credit metrics (CP-1) for Victory Capital Holdings, Inc. (ticker VCTR), as of 2026-11-05 (cutoff 2026-11-05), pathway credit_snapshot, public case. Reporting currency: USD. The filings state USD in thousands, except per-share data and the narrative sections that state US$ millions; this handoff keeps figures in US$ thousands as printed in the statements, and gives the four chart tables in US$ millions (one thousand US$ thousands equals one US$ million) or in multiples (x). Perimeter: Victory Capital Holdings, Inc. consolidated with its wholly-owned subsidiaries; Victory is both the filer and the borrower, so there is no subsidiary issuer inside a combined filing and no parent-versus-issuer split to make. Current period Q3 2026 (three months and nine months ended 2026-09-30); prior period FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), with FY2024 and the nine months and quarter of 2025 as comparatives. LTM means the twelve months to the stated quarter, calculated as FY2025 plus the 2026 year-to-date figure less the 2025 year-to-date figure; every LTM figure is a calculation, not a reported figure. The upstream readiness handoff (CP-0) carried forward its limitations: no credit agreement, no First Eagle financing documents, no ratings, no covenant ratio.

## Findings

| Gross debt to last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA fell from 1.44x at FY2025 to 1.14x at Q3 2026, helped by a full year of the Amundi US business. | Standalone leverage is low, but leverage after the First Eagle deal is unknown. | Medium |

| Liquidity at September 30, 2026 is cash of 207.724 million dollars plus an undrawn 100.0 million dollar revolver. | Near-term liquidity is ample against a term loan with no bullet until September 2032. | High |

### Financial base view

The financial base is usable for a credit snapshot of the standalone company at September 30, 2026, with the following boundaries. The statements are consolidated and complete for the annual report and the three quarterly reports; every reported figure in the tables below is taken from a statement page, and the adjusted EBITDA reconciliations are the company's own. Debt is one instrument family: the term loan under the 2019 Credit Agreement, 975,150 thousand dollars of principal at September 30, 2026, with a 100.0 million dollar revolver that is undrawn. Standalone leverage on the company's adjusted EBITDA is low and has fallen across the four periods tested, and cash interest is covered many times; both results lean on a management EBITDA that adds back share-based compensation, acquisition and restructuring costs, so the same ratios are shown on a stricter proxy. The base cannot support three conclusions: the covenant headroom (the ratio is not reported), the capital structure after the pending First Eagle acquisition (no amounts, no financing terms), and any ratings or market view (none supplied). LTM figures are calculated, not reported, and the fiscal 2025 column carries only three quarters of the Amundi US business, which closed on April 1, 2025, so the FY2025 ratios are not comparable with the LTM ratios without that caveat.

### Capital structure and debt terms

- Instrument: term loan under the 2019 Credit Agreement, principal 975,150 at September 30, 2026 (982,538 at December 31, 2025), maturing September 23, 2032, amortizing 1% a year of the 985.0 million dollar original principal in quarterly installments. Q3-10Q page:20 shows the table "Due September 2032$975,150" with an interest rate of 5.82% and an effective rate of 5.98%. Carrying value is 965,911 net of unamortized issuance costs of 3,014 and discount of 6,225 (Q3-10Q page:20).

- Pricing: after the Seventh Amendment of May 18, 2026 the margin is SOFR plus 1.75% (alternate base rate plus 0.75%); the company elects three-month Term SOFR (Q3-10Q page:20). Before it, SOFR plus 2.00% (10-K page:142). Interest rates are floating; the swap was terminated on October 30, 2023, and its deferred gain is being amortized as a credit to interest expense through September 23, 2032 (Q3-10Q page:25), which makes reported interest expense lower than cash interest in each period; the unamortized balance at December 31, 2025 was 11.7 million dollars before tax (10-K page:145).

- Revolver: 100.0 million dollar commitment with a 10.0 million dollar letter-of-credit sublimit, maturing September 23, 2030, undrawn at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025 (Q3-10Q page:44). No letter of credit is shown as using it at September 30, 2026: the liquidity table prints an undrawn commitment equal to the full 100,000 (Q3-10Q page:43).

- Ranking and parties: the revolver is described as first lien; the borrower is Victory Capital Holdings, Inc.; the guarantors and collateral package are Not supplied (the filings refer only to "the other loan parties"). No other debt instrument, bond, finance lease or off-balance-sheet debt is printed in the balance sheet or debt notes.
- Total debt per the Q3 earnings release is "approximately $975 million" (R3 page:4), which agrees with the gross principal in the note; the balance sheet shows the net carrying amount.
### Claims outside the debt figure

- Operating leases: operating lease liabilities of 42,405 at September 30, 2026 (Q3-10Q page:5) and 45,610 at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:149); all leases are operating leases (10-K page:149). They are outside the debt figure used in leverage. Adjusted EBITDA adds back depreciation but not lease cost, so lease expense (operating lease cost 8,955 in FY2025, 10-K page:149) stays inside EBITDA.

- Contingent consideration (WestEnd): 53,760 at September 30, 2026, estimated payable over the next year, maximum 80.0 million dollars potentially payable (Q3-10Q page:45); outside debt; paid 39,943 in cash during the nine months of 2026 (Q3-10Q page:8).

- Preferred stock: 20,037 thousand shares of preferred stock issued and outstanding at September 30, 2026 (Q3-10Q page:5), issued to Amundi in the Amundi US acquisition; preferred stock dividends of 29,806 in the nine months of 2026 (Q3-10Q page:5). Outside debt, but a fixed-charge-like claim ahead of common equity; the redemption terms are Not supplied.

- Pensions and retiree medical: the company reports a defined contribution 401(k) plan (10-K page:150); no defined benefit plan, pension or retiree medical obligation was located. A deferred compensation plan liability of 80,636 at December 31, 2025 is matched by plan investments of 98,758 in a rabbi trust whose assets are available to general creditors in bankruptcy (10-K pages:107 and 150); in the Q3 10-Q these are folded into other liabilities and investments.
- Purchase commitments, factoring, supply-chain finance and tax receivable agreements: a search of the 10-K and the Q3 10-Q for these terms found none, so none is reported here.

- Litigation: the 10-K states the company "is not currently a party to any material legal proceedings" (10-K page:152); the Q3 10-Q discloses two stockholder complaints and ten demand letters about the First Eagle proxy statement, with no loss estimate (Q3-10Q page:48).

- Regulatory capital: the broker-dealer subsidiary is subject to the net capital rule and its cash is "generally not available for corporate purposes" (10-K page:152); the split of consolidated cash is Not supplied.
### Liquidity

Liquidity is cash plus undrawn committed facilities, net of letters of credit drawn on them, by facility. Facility one is the revolver: commitment 100.0 US$m, drawn 0, letters of credit drawn on it none shown, available 100.000 US$m, expiry September 23, 2030 (not within twelve months). Cash is 207.724 US$m. Total 307.724 US$m at September 30, 2026 (calculated), against 263.690 at December 31, 2025, 175.849 at March 31, 2026 and 170.126 at June 30, 2026. Total liquidity rose from 170.126 at June 30, 2026 to 307.724 at September 30, 2026, because cash rose from 70.126 to 207.724 while the revolver stayed undrawn. Known near-term calls are the contingent consideration of 53.8 US$m, the quarterly term loan installment of about 2.46 US$m, the dividend of 0.50 dollars per common share payable December 23, 2026 (Q3-10Q page:25), and any First Eagle cash consideration, which is Not supplied. The balance sheet shows no separate restricted cash line; the regulated-subsidiary constraint above is the only limit on cash availability that the filings describe.
### Covenants

The 2019 Credit Agreement carries one financial maintenance covenant: a first lien leverage ratio of no greater than 4.00 to 1.00, tested at the end of each fiscal quarter only when revolver borrowings exceed 35.0% of commitments (Q3-10Q page:20). With a 100.0 million dollar commitment the test is not triggered unless more than 35.0 million dollars is drawn (calculated), and the revolver is undrawn. There is no step-down printed. The company states it was in compliance at September 30, 2026. The reported covenant ratio, the covenant definition of EBITDA and first lien debt, and any add-back cap are Not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable. For orientation only, gross term loan principal over the calculated LTM adjusted EBITDA is 1.14x; this is not the covenant metric, because the covenant is defined on first lien debt and a covenant EBITDA that is not in the pack.
### Definition risks in EBITDA

Adjusted EBITDA (US$ thousands) is the company's measure: 856,348 on an LTM basis against 727,102 for the stricter proxy of income from operations plus depreciation and amortization, a calculated difference of 129,246 that rests on the reconciliation's addbacks and is not decomposed here. The addbacks include share-based compensation, which the footnote describes as "associated with equity awards in connection with acquisitions and certain one-time performance-based shares" (Q3-10Q page:43), acquisition, restructuring and exit costs, other business taxes, and debt issuance costs. The share-based compensation addback is 32,547 in Q3 2026 against 2,022 in Q3 2025 (Q3-10Q page:42), and the filings do not separate the one-time part. On the proxy, leverage at September 30, 2026 is 1.34x gross and 1.06x net, against 1.14x and 0.90x on adjusted EBITDA. Both are far below the 4.00x covenant level, but that level is a different metric. Pro forma Amundi US data is given only for revenue and net income, not EBITDA (Q3-10Q page:12), so no pro forma EBITDA exists in the pack.
### Cash flow quality and uses of cash

Net cash provided by operating activities was 479,740 in the nine months of 2026 against 240,409 in the nine months of 2025 (Q3-10Q page:8); the 2025 period contains only six months of Amundi US. Cash taxes paid were 102,958 against 55,266, and cash interest 41,456 against 63,386. Calculated uses of that operating cash in the nine months of 2026: dividends paid 123,943, repurchases of common stock 225,207, taxes paid on net share settlement of equity awards 54,119 and contingent consideration paid 39,943, together 443,212 (calculated), against operating cash flow of 479,740 and capital expenditure of 3,024. Net term loan repayment in the period was 7,388 (payments of 313,969 less proceeds of 306,581 around the repricing of May 18, 2026). The direction of capital allocation is therefore towards equity holders, with debt reduced only by the scheduled amortization; repayments of 2.5 million dollars in Q3 2026 and 7.4 million dollars in the nine months are stated in Q3-10Q page:21. Quarterly cash flow figures are not in the pack, so Q3 columns for cash flow lines are n/a, and the Q3 release's quarterly operating cash flow is not used.
### Latest quarter and subsequent events

- Q3 2026 revenue was 396,573 against 361,195 in Q3 2025 (Q3-10Q page:5) and, per the release, lower than the second quarter of 2026 "primarily due to the crystallization of certain annual fees received in the second quarter" (R3 page:3). Income from operations was 137,723 against 138,126, so operating income was flat on higher revenue because operating expenses rose (258,850 against 223,069, Q3-10Q page:5), including acquisition-related costs of 15,529 in Q3 2026 against 379 (Q3-10Q page:5).

- First Eagle: on August 25, 2026 the company agreed to acquire GC Ferry Holdings, Inc. ("First Eagle") by a two-step merger; consideration is "a combination of cash, newly issued shares of the Company’s common stock, and newly issued shares of a new series of the Company’s non-voting convertible preferred stock"; a debt commitment letter provides financing "to fund the cash portion of the consideration and related fees and expenses"; closing is expected by the end of the first quarter of 2027, subject to stockholder approval, regulatory approvals and client consents (Q3-10Q pages:12 and 13). No amount of consideration, cash, new debt, commitment size or pricing is disclosed in the pack. Stockholder litigation and demand letters followed the proxy filings (Q3-10Q pages:47 and 48).
- Repricing: the Seventh Amendment of May 18, 2026 repriced the term loan; costs of 2.4 million dollars, of which 2.0 million dollars is a loss on debt extinguishment (Q3-10Q page:21).
- Dividend: a quarterly dividend of 0.50 dollars per share approved on November 4, 2026, payable December 23, 2026 (Q3-10Q page:25).
- Nothing in the pack is dated after the cutoff of 2026-11-05.
### Consistency with the earlier handoff

This handoff agrees with CP-0 on every point it checked and corrects none of it. It adopts CP-0's treatment of the Q3 MD&A text on "Existing Term Loans" as stale and takes the balance from Note 10; it takes the Q1 term loan principal from the Q1 note (980,075), not from the Q1 MD&A sentence with the unit error. It does derive an implied fourth quarter 2025 adjusted EBITDA of 197,476 and cash interest of 16,286 (FY2025 less the nine months of 2025), but only inside the LTM bridges, not as reported quarterly figures.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Victory is a fee-based, asset-based manager with eight investment franchises and a Solutions Platform. Amundi became a 26.1% fully diluted holder in 2025. The pending First Eagle acquisition is the key open credit event. | Medium | The merger agreement, financing commitment and amounts for First Eagle are not in the pack. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Revenue depends on assets under management and the fee rate; fund advisory contracts can be ended on short notice. | Earnings follow markets and flows, so revenue visibility is limited. | High |
| Amundi is both a large shareholder and the exclusive offshore distributor, with two board nominees. | A single partner carries ownership, distribution and governance weight. | High |
| Operating cost is described by management as about two-thirds variable, with minimal capital spending. | Margins may flex with revenue, which supports cash conversion. | Medium |
| First Eagle is expected to close by the end of the first quarter of 2027 for cash, shares and new preferred stock. | New debt size and leverage after closing cannot be judged yet. | High |
### Business and transaction view

Victory Capital is a diversified, asset-based investment manager whose credit profile rests on three things the sources document. First, a fee-on-assets revenue model: revenue moves with average assets under management, the fee rate and net flows, and fund advisory agreements are cancellable on short notice, so revenue is recurring in form but not contractually locked. Second, a multi-franchise, centralized-platform structure that management says keeps about two-thirds of operating expense variable and capital spending minimal, which supports cash conversion but depends on the investment teams being retained. Third, a strategic relationship with Amundi that is at once shareholder, board-nominating party, exclusive offshore distributor and exclusive supplier of Amundi's active products into the United States, which concentrates ownership, distribution and governance in one counterparty. The consolidated company's only debt is one term loan with an undrawn revolver (CP-1); ownership has no sponsor named, but no controlling-holder register is in the pack beyond Amundi and employee ownership. The transaction that matters most to a creditor is the pending acquisition of First Eagle for cash, common shares and a new series of non-voting convertible preferred stock, financed in part by a debt commitment letter whose amount and terms are not in the pack. All views here are on the standalone, pre-First Eagle company, and every First Eagle consequence is a gap, not a conclusion.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The Amundi US transaction closed on April 1, 2025. In exchange for all the shares of Amundi's U.S. business, Victory issued 3,293,471 shares of common stock and 19,698,274 shares of preferred stock (net of 44,026 preferred shares forfeited in a post-closing adjustment on August 1, 2025, per 10-K page:109), together 26.1% of fully diluted shares; the purchase price was approximately 1,326 US$ million, settled entirely in Company shares (Q3-10Q page:11). The 10-K exhibit index lists a certificate of designations for Series A Non-Voting Convertible Preferred Stock, and Amundi may require Victory to nominate two Amundi designees to the board (10-K page:135). Alongside the equity, Victory and Amundi entered exclusive distribution agreements, a 15-year exclusive offshore distribution arrangement that auto-renews in 2040 (10-K page:14). The purchase price allocation was finalized in Q1 2026 (Q3-10Q page:12). Pioneer Investments contributed revenue of about 155 US$ million in Q3 2026 and 517 US$ million in nine months 2026, and the filing states that net income attributable to Pioneer is "impractical to determine" because discrete franchise-level financial information is not prepared (Q3-10Q page:12). The Amundi deal is a completed transaction, so for creditors it explains the 2025 jump in assets and in goodwill and intangibles, not a new financing event.

Debt events in the period are refinancings, not new money. On September 23, 2025 the Sixth Amendment extended the revolver to September 23, 2030 and repriced the term loan at 985.0 US$ million; on May 18, 2026 the Seventh Amendment repriced the term loan to SOFR plus 1.75% (Q2-10Q page:18; Q3-10Q page:20). No bond, note or other new debt issue appears in the pack. Costs of the Seventh Amendment were 2.4 US$ million, of which 2.0 US$ million was a loss on debt extinguishment (Q3-10Q page:21).

The pending First Eagle transaction, all of it a subsequent event relative to the Q2 2026 reports and still pending at the cutoff, is described in the Q3 2026 report: on August 25, 2026 Victory agreed to acquire GC Ferry Holdings, Inc. from GC Ferry Parent, L.P. through a two-step merger; consideration is a combination of cash, newly issued common stock and a new series of non-voting convertible preferred stock; Victory entered a debt commitment letter with certain financial institutions to fund the cash portion and related fees; closing is expected by the end of the first quarter of 2027, subject to approval by Victory stockholders, regulatory approvals and client consents (Q3-10Q pages:12 and 13). Management calls it "transformational" and says it adds a scaled CLO and alternative credit platform (R3 page:2), which is Management Language. For a creditor the mechanics are: cash consideration funded by new debt raises leverage from the current low standalone level by an amount that is not disclosed; new preferred stock adds a senior-to-common claim, as the Amundi preferred already is; share issuance dilutes and may shift control, and the closing depends on stockholder and client consents, so completion risk and the post-closing capital structure are both open. Transaction costs already expensed were 15.5 US$ million in Q3 2026 and 22.5 US$ million in nine months 2026 (Q3-10Q page:13). Litigation followed the proxy: two stockholder complaints and ten demand letters seek, among other things, to enjoin closing until more disclosure is made (Q3-10Q page:48); Victory calls them without merit and gives no loss estimate. No amount of consideration, cash portion, commitment size, lenders, pricing, ticking fees or conditions of the financing is in the pack, and no First Eagle financial statements are supplied, so the new debt issue, pro forma leverage, and pro forma liquidity are Not supplied and Not calculable. Dated after the Q3 reporting period but inside the cutoff: the definitive proxy statement (October 16, 2026) and the dividend of 0.50 dollars per share approved on November 4, 2026.

### Credit translations

1. Evidence: fund advisory agreements terminable on not more than 60 days' notice (10-K page:26), and revenues that "are based on the level of client assets we manage" (10-K page:16). Mechanic: assets can be withdrawn or fall with markets with little notice, so fee revenue and EBITDA fall quickly. Implication: debt service capacity is high today but is exposed to a market or performance shock; monitoring posture should track monthly flows and AUM. Counter: management says about two-thirds of operating expense is variable, which dampens margin impact.

2. Evidence: Amundi as 26.1% fully diluted holder, two board nominees, exclusive distribution (Q3-10Q page:11; 10-K page:135, page:14). Mechanic: one counterparty influences ownership, governance and the offshore revenue channel; a dispute or change could affect distribution and strategic direction. Implication: key uncertainty on counterparty dependence; creditor control is not affected as there is no sponsor, but equity ownership is partly in a preferred class with its own terms Not supplied.

3. Evidence: pending First Eagle acquisition with a debt commitment letter and cash consideration (Q3-10Q pages:12 and 13); CP-1 shows low standalone leverage on a single term loan. Mechanic: cash funded by new debt will raise debt service and leverage by an undisclosed amount, while preferred issuance adds a claim ranking ahead of common; the benefit depends on integration and net flows of an acquired platform. Implication: leverage tolerance after closing is the central open question; committee readiness is limited until the financing documents are in the pack. Counter: the conflict log has no direct conflict on the First Eagle terms, but absence of amounts is itself the limitation.

4. Evidence: net flows swung from outflow to inflow (R1 page:1; R3 page:2) and Q3 2026 revenue fell against Q2 2026 on annual fee timing (R3 page:3). Mechanic: quarterly revenue is volatile around performance and annual fees. Implication: use LTM rather than single-quarter EBITDA for any ratio, as CP-1 does.

It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Before the First Eagle acquisition, Victory's debt is small against its earnings: 1.14x gross and 0.90x net of last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA, with 14.83x cash interest cover. The credit view after closing is open. | Medium | First Eagle financing amounts and terms are not in the sources, and covenant headroom cannot be calculated. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Debt is one term loan of USD 975.15 million, due September 23, 2032, with an undrawn USD 100.0 million revolver. | There is no large maturity before 2032 and no revolver draw to refinance. | High |

| Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was USD 307.724 million, from cash of USD 207.724 million plus the revolver. | Near-term obligations are covered several times over by cash and the undrawn facility. | High |

| Revenue follows assets under management and fee rates, and fund advisory contracts can be ended on 60 days' notice. | Earnings can fall quickly in a market or performance shock, even though costs partly flex. | High |

| First Eagle is expected to close by the end of the first quarter of 2027, with new debt of undisclosed size. | Leverage and ranking after closing cannot be judged until the financing is known. | High |
### Credit view

Victory Capital's standalone credit profile is sound on every measure the sources allow, but the credit view after the First Eagle acquisition is open. The strongest support is balance sheet and cash generation: USD 975.15 million of term loan against USD 856.348 million of last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA (1.14x gross, 0.90x net), cash interest cover of 14.83x, USD 307.724 million of liquidity and a first maturity of any size in September 2032. The weakest point is that earnings are fee income on assets that clients can withdraw on short notice, and a large cash-and-shares acquisition is pending whose debt, terms and target financials are not in the sources. What decides the outcome is the size and pricing of the First Eagle financing, whether closing happens as planned, and whether net inflows persist after the record third quarter of 2026.
### Key findings

1. The standalone balance sheet carries one debt instrument, the term loan under the 2019 Credit Agreement of USD 975.15 million at September 30, 2026, alongside an undrawn USD 100.0 million revolver, described as first lien, maturing September 23, 2030 [CP-1 capital structure]. The interest rate is 5.82%, floating at SOFR plus 1.75% since the May 18, 2026 repricing. Leverage on management's adjusted EBITDA fell from 1.44x at FY2025 to 1.14x at the last twelve months to Q3 2026 [CP-1 leverage chart]; the fall comes from higher EBITDA (USD 682.851 million to USD 856.348 million) and from the FY2025 figure including only three quarters of the Amundi US business, which means the comparison flatters the improvement. On the stricter proxy of operating income plus depreciation and amortization (USD 727.102 million), leverage is 1.34x gross and 1.06x net [CP-1 definition risks]. Either way leverage is far under the single covenant level of 4.00x, but that covenant is defined on first lien debt and a covenant EBITDA that are not in the sources, so headroom is Not calculable.

2. Cash interest cover rose from 8.57x at FY2025 to 14.83x on the last twelve months [CP-1 interest cover chart], and part of that rise is the last-twelve-months window dropping an unexplained third quarter of 2025 cash interest payment of USD 30.025 million. Third quarter of 2026 cash interest was USD 13.696 million, so the last-twelve-months cash interest of USD 57.742 million is not out of line with the recent quarterly pace.

3. Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was USD 307.724 million against USD 170.126 million at June 30, 2026. The change is cash: USD 207.724 million against USD 70.126 million, with the revolver unchanged [CP-1 liquidity]. Calls on it include USD 53.8 million of contingent consideration for the WestEnd acquisition estimated payable within a year, quarterly term loan amortization of about USD 2.46 million, the dividend of USD 0.50 a share payable December 23, 2026, and the unknown cash portion of First Eagle. Part of consolidated cash sits in a regulated broker-dealer whose cash is generally not available for corporate purposes [CP-1 claims outside debt]; the split is Not supplied.

4. Cash generation is strong but is allocated to equity holders. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 621.193 million over the last twelve months [CP-1 calculations], 0.64x of gross debt (calculated below). In nine months 2026 dividends, repurchases, taxes on net share settlement and contingent payments used USD 443.212 million of USD 479.74 million operating cash flow, 92.4% (calculated below), and net term loan repayment was USD 7.388 million [CP-1 cash flow]. This is Analyst Interpretation: nothing in the sources shows these distributions funded by debt, and no creditor-adverse action is documented [CP-1A governance], but the credit agreement's restricted payment terms are not supplied, so legal capacity to distribute is unknown.

5. The business model concentrates risk in assets and people rather than in assets on the balance sheet. Revenue is fees on assets; fund advisory contracts are terminable on not more than 60 days' notice; the largest franchise, Pioneer Investments, was acquired from Amundi and sits at about the 42% ceiling the company states; Amundi is also a 26.1% fully diluted holder with two board nomination rights and the exclusive offshore distributor [CP-1A operating model; ownership]. Management says about two-thirds of operating expense is variable, a Management Language claim, but personnel compensation rose in the third quarter of 2026, so the cushion is not proved [CP-1A operating model].

6. First Eagle changes the credit profile. Consideration is cash, new common stock and a new series of non-voting convertible preferred stock, funded in part under a debt commitment letter; closing is expected by the end of the first quarter of 2027, subject to stockholder, regulatory and client approvals; stockholder litigation seeks to delay it [CP-1A transaction summary]. No amounts are given. Any post-closing leverage, liquidity, ranking or covenant statement is Not calculable and is withheld.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. (1) Low standalone leverage and strong cover on the sources' own measures, Documentary Fact from the CP-1 tables, with the caveat that adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that adds back share-based compensation and acquisition costs; the stricter proxy still gives a leverage level well within the covenant level. (2) A long, simple debt structure: one term loan to September 23, 2032, amortizing 1% a year, with calculated annual maturities of USD 9.85 million before the bullet of about USD 918.5 million, and a revolver to September 23, 2030 that is undrawn (Documentary Fact for the dates, Analyst Interpretation for the calculated schedule). (3) Liquidity of USD 307.724 million, with minimal capital spending of USD 3.024 million in nine months 2026 (Documentary Fact). (4) Scale and diversity across eight investment franchises, a Solutions Platform and four client channels, with the largest franchise at about 42% of assets under management (Documentary Fact). (5) Net inflows in the second and third quarters of 2026 after outflows in the first quarter of 2026 and in the nine months of 2025: USD 11.702 billion of long-term net inflows in the third quarter of 2026 (Management Language for "record", Documentary Fact for the amount).

Weaknesses. (1) Revenue visibility is short because fund advisory contracts can be ended on 60 days' notice and revenue moves with markets, flows and fee realization, which fell to 44.8 bp in the third quarter of 2026 from 47.9 bp in the second quarter (Documentary Fact). (2) Reliance on Amundi for ownership, board seats and offshore distribution concentrates a single counterparty (Documentary Fact); the Amundi preferred stock terms are Not supplied. (3) The pending First Eagle acquisition with undisclosed debt and a cash component creates leverage, execution and litigation risk (Documentary Fact for existence; the credit effect is Insufficient Information). (4) Earnings quality: adjusted EBITDA exceeds the proxy by USD 129.246 million (15.1% of adjusted EBITDA, calculated below), and the share-based compensation addback jumped in the third quarter of 2026 without the one-time part being separated (Documentary Fact). (5) Distributions to equity absorb most operating cash flow, leaving debt reduction at the scheduled amount (Analyst Interpretation). (6) Absent monitoring data: covenant ratio, guarantors and collateral, restricted payment capacity and ratings (Insufficient Information).
### Assessment and thesis

| Thesis | A fee-income asset manager with a single long-dated term loan and strong cash generation is sound today, but its creditworthiness depends on how much debt First Eagle adds and whether inflows persist | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Same basis plus CP-1A operating model |

Confidence is below High because CP-1A judged this module Ready with limitations and logged High-severity gaps on the First Eagle documents; the financial inputs themselves are from audited and filed statements.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Basis |

| New debt for First Eagle | Cash portion funded under a commitment letter raises debt by an undisclosed amount against a standalone term loan of USD 975.15 million | Leverage tolerance and ranking after closing are unknown; monitoring posture is to withhold a post-deal view | Material | CP-1A transaction summary; CP-1 capital structure |

| Market and flow shock | Fees fall with assets under management; contracts can be ended on 60 days' notice; Q3 2026 market action was negative USD 2.2 billion | Debt service capacity falls with revenue, partly offset by variable cost | Material | CP-1A operating model |

| Amundi dependence | Shareholder, board nominator, exclusive distributor and largest franchise origin | Disruption in the relationship affects distribution and governance together | Material | CP-1A ownership and governance; transaction summary |

| Shareholder distributions | Dividends and buybacks absorb most of operating cash flow while credit agreement limits are not known | Unknown legal capacity to distribute more if a deal is delayed or markets weaken | Minor | CP-1 cash flow; CP-1A governance |

| Earnings measure | Adjusted EBITDA adds back share-based compensation and acquisition costs | Leverage and cover look better than on the proxy; covenant EBITDA unknown | Minor | CP-1 definition risks |

| Interest-rate exposure | Term loan floats on SOFR and the swap has been terminated, though deferred gain still lowers reported interest expense | Cash interest can rise with rates; cover is high so the effect is small | Minor | CP-1 capital structure |
